screening_decisions.reason: Double-blind trial of theophylline/aminophylline versus placebo in acute ischemic stroke/cerebral infarction. Treatment was started in the acute phase, consistent with inclusion criteria.
Double-blind placebo-controlled trial of intravenous aminophylline in acute cerebral infarction. Aminophylline is an analogue compound and the study fits the acute stroke timing requirement.
Open-label, single-arm dose-escalation safety study; not a randomized placebo/control trial.
Not clearly a randomized acute ischemic stroke trial; focuses on cerebral metabolism in mixed subjects rather than the target clinical question.
Randomized crossover physiologic study in patients recovering from stroke, not a therapeutic trial of theophylline or an analogue for acute ischemic stroke.
Physiologic crossover study focused on blood flow, not an acute stroke treatment randomized trial meeting the criteria.
Cerebral circulation physiology study, not a randomized placebo/control trial in acute ischemic stroke patients.
Animal experiment in cats, not a human randomized stroke trial.
Dog cardiovascular pharmacology study, not a clinical trial in acute ischemic stroke.
Mechanistic/background discussion, not a randomized acute ischemic stroke trial.
